title: Experiment: a Node-only module across the Server/Client boundary, guarded and unguarded
summary: A `lib/planning.js` using `node:fs`, `node:child_process` and a lock-shaped API, imported four ways under `next build`. Imported by a Server Component it built and rendered the value, with and without a `server-only` marker. Imported by a `'use client'` component it failed both times — but differently: UNGUARDED the build failed with `Error: Failed to write app endpoint /page`, `type: 'TurbopackInternalError'`, `location: undefined`, naming no file; GUARDED it failed at `./lib/planning.js:1:1` with the offending source line, a caret, an explanation and a docs link.

facts.layout: lib/ as a sibling of app/, plain relative import
facts.workspace: disposable, rebuilt per case, removal verified

omissions.reason: The build never completed, so there is no server to observe. Whether a different bundler configuration would have produced a running app with a broken client chunk was not explored.
Turbopack is the default at 16.3.2 and was the only builder exercised. The unguarded failure mode is a Turbopack internal error and may differ under webpack.

notes: ⚠️ THE CONTRAST IS THE FINDING, not the failure. Both client cases fail, so a probe that only asked 'is it prevented' would have reported success for both and concluded the marker was optional — which is what the Next.js documentation says. What separates them is whether anyone can tell WHY: `TurbopackInternalError` with `location: undefined` is indistinguishable from a bundler bug. ⚠️ MESSAGE ACCURACY CAVEAT, recorded because it would mislead: in the guarded direct-import case Next.js said "you are using it in the Pages Router" — this project uses the App Router, and the wording is simply wrong. The adapter case (EVD-0050) produced the correct App Router message. The diagnostic is locatable either way; its prose is not always right.
